sources.title: Coder Agents overview
sources.locator: index.md How it works; Built-in tools; Plan mode; LLM providers; Security benefits
sources.finding: Chat interface and API for delegating work to a self-hosted Go agent that runs inside the Coder control plane; workspaces provisioned automatically from templates; sub-agents; queueing; attachments; providers Anthropic, OpenAI, Google, Azure, Bedrock, OpenAI-compatible, OpenRouter, Vercel; no SaaS component.

sources.title: Coder Agents architecture
sources.finding: Agent loop in control plane; chat state in the database; context compaction (/compact); actions attributed to the submitting user.

sources.title: Coder Agents licensing and usage
sources.locator: Community and Premium licenses; AI Premium; Agent Time; usage reporting
sources.finding: Community and Premium: up to five concurrently active agents deployment-wide, queued beyond; AI Premium: unlimited concurrent agents against purchased Agent Hours; usage hours reported to Coder Tallyman/Metronome without chat data.

sources.title: Getting started
sources.finding: Admin configures an LLM provider and model per organization; needs a template; every org member can use Agents by default; CI/webhook triggering listed as API use.

sources.title: Models
sources.locator: Model configuration; user API keys (BYOK); personal model overrides
sources.finding: Admin-managed providers and per-organization models; optional user API keys per provider; model identifiers such as claude-opus-4-6 and gpt-5.3-codex.

sources.title: Platform controls
sources.locator: Design philosophy; Providers and models; System prompt
sources.finding: All agent configuration is admin-level and enforced server-side; templates, MCP servers, retention and budgets controlled centrally.

sources.title: Spend management
sources.finding: Per-user and group monthly budgets enforced through AI Gateway (requires entitlement); native cost tracking removed; limit cap $1,000,000 per member per period.

sources.title: Network isolation
sources.locator: How it works; Configure the template
sources.finding: Template-defined separate pod for the agent with network policy; early stage; user pod unrestricted; bubblewrap suggested as alternative.

sources.title: ACP subagents
sources.finding: Experimental: with chat-acp-subagents experiment, external harnesses such as Claude Code or Codex run as ACP subagents in the workspace, using the harness own credentials; tool permission requests auto-approved; not in plan mode.

sources.title: Chat sharing
sources.locator: Share a chat; Shared chat access
sources.finding: Share read-only with users or groups; viewers cannot send messages; admins can disable sharing.

sources.title: Projects
sources.finding: Early access: project instructions, skills and memory shared across chats; private to owner; changes in audit log.

sources.title: Extending agents
sources.locator: Workspace shares context; Where the agent looks
sources.finding: Workspace agent scans for AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, .cursorrules, skills and .mcp.json and pushes a snapshot that chats pin; refresh context control.

sources.title: Conversation data retention
sources.finding: Archived chats purged after a configurable retention period (default 30 days, can be disabled); auto-archive separate.

sources.title: Advisor
sources.finding: Experimental chat-advisor lets a root agent request a single-step model call for strategic guidance.

sources.title: Git providers
sources.finding: In-chat diff viewer and merge request status use configured external auth for GitHub and GitLab; write_repository scope allows pushing commits and creating merge requests.

sources.title: Chat search syntax
sources.finding: Chat search filters include pr_status (draft/open/merged/closed/none) for linked pull requests.

sources.title: Chat limits
sources.finding: Deployment chat limits: MaxStepsPerTurn, MaxGenerationRetries, MaxQueuedMessagesPerChat, MaxAttachmentsPerChat, MaxPromptBytes, MaxConcurrentRecordingUploads, configurable through deployment options.

sources.title: LLM retry logic
sources.finding: Transient provider errors are classified (overloaded, rate limit, timeout, stream silence timeout, usage limit, auth, config) and retried with exponential backoff from 1s capped at 60s, honoring provider retry hints.

sources.title: execute tool
sources.finding: The execute tool waits 10s by default (timeout argument up to the caller), supports run_in_background and a wait_timeout override; no approval prompt appears in the tool.

sources.title: Agents page mobile handling
sources.locator: site/src/pages/AgentsPage/hooks/useConversationEditingState.ts lines 3 and 137; useAgentChatPanelPreference.ts line 2; 91 sm:/md:/lg: Tailwind class uses across AgentsPage (rg -c)
sources.finding: The Agents page imports isMobileViewport and useMediaQuery and applies responsive classes, so the web UI adapts to narrow viewports in code; no documentation states supported phone browsers.

sources.title: chatd architecture notes
sources.finding: Receivers must tolerate duplicate pubsub deliveries and the run loop deduplicates state updates; duplicate execution of tool calls after an interruption is not addressed.

sources.title: Agent loop and sub-agents in chatd
sources.finding: chatd implements spawn_agent sub-agents, ACP integration and admission control with default 5 concurrent root agents and 10 concurrent subagents.

sources.title: Chat HTTP routes
sources.finding: Authenticated REST endpoints under /api/v2/chats for list, create, watch, files, projects and model configs.

sources.title: coder exp chat CLI
sources.finding: coder CLI exposes experimental chat and workspace-context subcommands.

sources.title: Deployment feature flags
sources.finding: License features include agent_runtime_hours and ai_governance_user_limit for Agent Time and AI governance.

sources.title: AGPL-3.0 license
sources.finding: GNU Affero General Public License v3.0 at the repository root.

sources.title: Enterprise license
sources.finding: Enterprise-licensed code lives under enterprise/ (aiseats, audit, ai-gateway); core under AGPL-3.0.

sources.title: Telemetry
sources.finding: Coder collects telemetry from installations by default; CODER_TELEMETRY_ENABLE=false disables it.

sources.title: Coder MCP server
sources.finding: Built-in MCP server (stdio via CLI and remote HTTP with OAuth2) exposing workspace and template tools to other AI assistants.

sources.title: Bring your own MCP servers
sources.finding: Agents can use admin-approved external MCP servers and workspace .mcp.json servers.

sources.title: AI Gateway
sources.finding: Gateway for governing and metering model traffic with budgets and audit; entitlement-gated.

sources.title: Coder pricing
sources.finding: Community free (up to 5 active Coder Agents, AI Governance); Premium priced annually per user with no amount shown (adds Coder Agents, HA, audit logging, multi-org RBAC, OIDC sync, SLA); AI Premium custom (unlimited active agents, Coder Agents API for headless agents, network-isolated agent workspaces).

sources.title: Install the Coder CLI
sources.finding: Coder CLI installs on Linux, macOS and Windows; the control plane installs on Linux, Kubernetes and other hosts.

sources.title: In the IDE
sources.finding: Workspaces support IDE agents (Cursor, Copilot, Roo and others); developers connect via VS Code, JetBrains and other editors to review agent output.

sources.title: OIDC authentication
sources.finding: OIDC login documented for the Coder dashboard; group/role sync is a Premium feature (idp-sync).

sources.finding: Latest stable patch release at pass time; v2.39.x line current.
